title.narrative: National Democratic Institute- Elections Cap Build

description.narrative: Projektet ämnar åtgärda de problem som inhemska och internationella observatörer lyft som rör valprocessen. Detta projekt innebär forskning om allmänhetens förtroende för och inställning till valprocessen, stärka kapaciteten för analys och kartläggning av valresultat, utbildning av parterna valobservatörer och CEC valförrättare, etc.

The project will address concerns raised by domestic and international observers concerning the electoral process. This project entails research on public confidence in, and attitudes towards the electoral process, strenghtening the capacity for analysis and mapping of election results, training of parties election observers and CEC election officials, etc.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: •Through public opinion polling NDI addressed a deficit of accurate, unbiased political information. The quality of this information steadily improved over the years. •Public opinion polls became a benchmark not only for the government, political parties, media, NGOs and others but overall for the society. People follow the polls, they try to analyze and discuss trends. •Both political parties and media started using data in their work. •Polling helped to increase the level of messaging. Not necessarily coherent messaging but nevertheless messaging. •NDI’s work with the CEC improved the work of CEC’s Small Grants Commission by increasing the capacity of commission members and transparency of decisions made by the CEC’s Small Grants Commission. •NDI with the assistant of local NGOs (ISFED and GYLA) advocated that the CEC maintained a database of election commissioners that have violated election procedures or have been dismissed from their posts; also the administrative punishment for violations matched the severity of the transgression. •The project has set a completely different tone on women’s political participation in Georgia. It has contributed immensely to changing the reluctant attitude of political parties regarding gender issues to a more meaningful dialogue about empowering women within parties and establishing and building women’s organizations inside the parties. •The project set the ground for meaningful discussion about gender quotas with its work with civil society groups and political entities. •The project utilized a systematic approach to training women candidates from various political parties in a multi-party environment as well as worked with the candidates and their staff on individual bases utilizing public opinion poll results customized for each candidate’s majoritarian district.
